title: Lesson-archetype templates
summary: Five frozen lesson-archetype templates: Do-Now → I/We/You-Do (Rosenshine + explicit-instruction), 5-a-day Drill, Mini-Quiz Recap, Exit-Ticket, Worked-Example → Mini-Whiteboard → Independent Practice. Each is a pre-filled brief that the AI completes; teachers pick from a modal and the form state populates. Stamps metadata.lessonArchetype so the audit panel and downstream renderers can show 'Built from: <archetype>'.
motivation: Twinkl PlanIt is praised for 'lesson plans with detailed subject knowledge'. Most worksheet teachers want a structured lesson sequence, not a freeform sheet. Today the generator is freeform — teachers either get great rigour (when they specify well) or generic output (when they don't). Templates push every teacher to the rigour ceiling.

in: client/src/lib/lessonArchetypes.ts (new, ~200 LoC) — five frozen ArchetypeDefinition objects + buildArchetypeBrief(archetype, context) helper
client/src/components/ArchetypePickerDialog.tsx (new, ~150 LoC) — modal opened from a 'Use a template' button on the Worksheets generator form
client/src/lib/promptSections/archetypeDirectives.ts (new, ~100 LoC) — per-archetype prompt block injected into structuredSystemSections
client/src/components/AuditTrailPanel.tsx — surface metadata.lessonArchetype as a chip in the audit panel header
Targeted vitest: each archetype's buildArchetypeBrief output passes the existing post-validator chain
out: Custom-archetype editor (teachers can't define their own; that's a Phase H follow-up)

archetypes.name: Do-Now → I/We/You-Do
archetypes.structure: Section A: 3-question Do-Now retrieval. Section B: I-Do worked example (1). Section C: We-Do invitational (1-2). Section D: You-Do independent (5-7). Reflection.

archetypes.name: 5-a-day Drill
archetypes.structure: 5 mixed-skill questions of escalating difficulty (1+2+2+3+5 marks). No pre-amble. Reflection optional.

archetypes.name: Mini-Quiz Recap
archetypes.structure: 5-10 MCQ recap of the previous lesson's LO. Mark scheme included. Distractor pedagogy enforced via existing validator.

archetypes.name: Exit-Ticket
archetypes.structure: 3-5 stem-questions tagged to today's LO. Designed to be marked in 90 seconds. Self-reflection slot.

archetypes.name: Worked-Example → Mini-Whiteboard → Independent
archetypes.structure: Section A: full worked example. Section B: 4-6 mini-whiteboard prompts (short-answer). Section C: 6-8 independent practice. Mark scheme + reflection.

acceptance_criteria: Each archetype's prompt block instructs the LLM to emit the named structure; the existing section-question-counts validator passes for every fixture.
Picking an archetype pre-fills the Worksheets form state and shows a 'Template: <name>' chip on the form.
metadata.lessonArchetype is stamped before generation and surfaces in the audit-trail panel.
Mini-quiz-recap output passes the distractor-pedagogy validator (PR-3 / item #4) on ≥80% of test fixtures.
Worked-mini-independent output's worked-example section passes the cap-worked-example-steps validator.
tsc --noEmit clean; npm test passes; npm run eval:worksheets passes (no fixture regressions).

risk_register.risk: Archetype prompt block conflicts with the section-question-counts contract (7-7-5+1)
risk_register.mitigation: Each archetype's structure is encoded as section-target overrides via metadata.sectionTargetsOverride; section-question-counts validator already supports overrides via PostValidatorOptions.
Onboarding banner on the Worksheets page + the SendToMenu surfaces 'Want a template?' on first generate.

related: G4 — procedural activities (templates can include wordsearch / cloze sections)
G5 — 5-a-day builder (G3's '5-a-day' archetype is single-day; G5 is multi-week)
